node2vec extends node embeddings f(u) and f(v) to an edge feature representation g(u,v) by applying a binary operator to the two node vectors. The four standard operators are:

1. Average: g(u,v) = (f(u) + f(v)) / 2. This produces the elementwise mean of the two node embeddings.
2. Hadamard: g(u,v) = f(u) ⊙ f(v). This produces the elementwise product.
3. Weighted-L1: g(u,v) = |f(u) - f(v)|. This produces the elementwise absolute difference.
4. Weighted-L2: g(u,v) = |f(u) - f(v)|^2. This produces the elementwise squared difference.

These operators are used to convert node representations into edge representations for downstream edge-based prediction tasks such as link prediction. Among them, Hadamard is often reported as a strong default choice in node2vec-style edge classification settings, though the best operator can depend on the dataset and task.
